findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (including the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet) are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is attached, so protection against public ACLs or policies depends entirely on account defaults.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, so report objects can be overwritten or the whole bucket and contents destroyed with no recovery path or integrity trail.
No logging block is configured, so access to this data bucket is not recorded, preventing detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached to this bucket, so objects may be retrieved or written over plaintext HTTP.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true, allowing ledger export objects to be silently overwritten or irreversibly destroyed.
No server access logging is configured for this financial data bucket, leaving no audit record of reads or writes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket; the private canned ACL alone is the only barrier to exposure.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored artifacts are not encrypted by default policy.
No public access block is applied, leaving the bucket reliant on account-level settings to prevent public ACL or policy grants.
Operational runbooks, which frequently contain hostnames, procedures and occasionally credentials, are stored without any server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to runbook content are not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so public ACLs or bucket policies are not categorically blocked.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid canned ACL (apparently a corrupted "log-delivery-write"), so the access control on the audit log destination bucket is malformed; the intended log-delivery-write grant would also give the AWS LogDelivery group write access to the audit bucket.

force_destroy = true on the bucket that receives access logs allows the entire log history to be deleted along with the bucket, destroying forensic evidence and undermining tamper-evidence of the audit trail.
The audit log bucket has no public access block resource, so a future ACL or policy change could expose security logs publicly.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party business data or PII) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored unencrypted.
